name: Opus Quality Defensive
strategy: Low-beta quality/defensive core (healthcare, quality factor, min-vol, staples) with a small gold diversifier and a disciplined 8% short on semis to express 'AI-infra overextended' without dominating the book.

positions.thesis: The conviction position. Healthcare leads on every horizon (+3.4% 1m, +13.9% 3m, +23.9% 12m), trades above its 50d and 200d, is the cheapest large defensive sector, and the leadership is broad across pharma, managed care, biotech and devices rather than a single name. In a rotation from expensive long-duration tech into cheap cash-flow, this is the biggest and best-quality destination — so I am sizing it like a real view instead of a diversification slot.

Replaces QUAL as the quality-factor sleeve. Same factor — screens on return on capital, free cash flow and low leverage — but without the ~30% technology weight that made QUAL a de-rating megacap proxy (-0.6% 1m). SCHD returned +6.0% 1m, +15.2% 6m, +26.0% 12m and sits 12.4% above its 200-day. Quality that is actually defensive.

Min-vol core ballast, now carrying the whole low-volatility allocation after folding in the redundant SPLV sleeve. +2.3% 1m and above both moving averages. Preferred over SPLV because SPLV's heavy utilities tilt is a headwind with 10-year yields at 4.62% and rising (XLU -2.4% 1m).

Consumer staples: low-beta cash-flow ballast that is participating, not just defending (+3.5% 1m, above 50d and 200d). KO +7.8% 1m and +13.1% 3m, COST +5.0% and WMT +4.5% over five days as the rotation reaches the group.

The AI-infra overextension view, still sized as insurance rather than a bet. It has worked hard (SMH -20.2% 1m, -14.1% in five days) as the memory and foundry complex broke — MU -35%, INTC -38%, AMD -20%, TSM -18%. I am deliberately not adding: SMH is 15% below its 50-day but still 12% above its 200-day and +70% over twelve months, so this is a stretched correction inside a long-term uptrend and squeeze risk is real. Stop caps a squeeze, take-profit banks the gain if the bust extends.

reassessment_note: Unrestricted-retail resize (2026-07-30, free internet + no sizing caps): The tape is validating this mandate precisely — capital is rotating out of the AI-capex complex into cheap defensive cash-flow — so the fix is not to change the strategy but to stop diluting it. Three changes. (1) XLV 19% to 36%: healthcare is the single highest-conviction idea available to a defensive book right now, leading on 1m (+3.4%), 3m (+13.9%) and 12m (+23.9%), above both its 50- and 200-day, and broad across LLY/ABBV/MRK/JNJ/UNH/IBB rather than resting on one name. Free sizing exists for exactly this. (2) QUAL 18% to zero, replaced by SCHD 16%: QUAL is ~30% technology and returned -0.6% over the month while the defensives it was supposed to sit beside made money — it was selling me tech beta under a quality label. SCHD applies a return-on-capital and FCF/leverage screen without the AI-bubble exposure and beat it on every horizon (+15.2% 6m, +26.0% 12m). This keeps the quality-factor leg of the mandate and fixes the vehicle. (3) GLD 6% to zero and SPLV 11% folded into USMV. Gold is -22% over six months and below both moving averages; with TLT also -5.3% on the month, both traditional hedges have failed, and cash at 4% APY is the honest defensive ballast. SPLV and USMV are near-duplicate min-vol exposures, and SPLV's utilities tilt is a liability with yields rising (XLU -2.4% 1m), so I consolidated into the better-diversified one. I am holding the SMH short at 8% rather than pressing it: it has done its job, but SMH is 15% below its 50-day while still 12% above its 200-day, and adding to a short after a -20% month is how you get squeezed. Stops go on the short only — a defensive mandate must not stop out of its defensives into a drawdown. Turnover is ~60% at ~2bps/side, roughly 2.4bps of NAV, trivially worth it.
research_notes:
Pulled full price/trend history (1d/5d/1m/3m/6m/12m plus 50d & 200d moving-average position) for ~60 tickers via Yahoo chart data through the 2026-07-29 close. WebSearch budget was exhausted and most news sites returned 503/403, so the read is built from price action, which was unusually unambiguous.

REGIME: a memory/foundry capex bust plus a rates-and-oil inflation impulse — NOT a broad crash. MU -35.5% 1m, INTC -37.8%, AMD -20.4%, TSM -17.7%, SMH -20.2% (-14.1% in 5 days, -4.8% on 7/29). But NVDA only -2.5% 1m, AVGO -0.6%, MSFT +6.0%, AAPL +20.0%, META +4.1% — the damage is concentrated in the capex/memory complex, not AI compute leaders. SPY just -1.6% 1m, equal-weight RSP +1.3% 1m and +6.0% 3m, HYG -1.0% (no credit stress). VIX 20.7, +24% on the week. This is a rotation out of one crowded trade, not a systemic event.

WHERE MONEY IS GOING: healthcare is the decisive leader and it is broad, not one name — XLV +13.9% 3m/+23.9% 12m, VHT +14.3% 3m, LLY +29.5%, ABBV +24.6%, MRK +19.4%, JNJ +15.5%, UNH +13.5%, IBB +11.8%, PPH +11.4%, IHI +7.9% in 5d. XLV sits +6.8% over its 50d and +9.2% over its 200d. Also bid: staples (XLP +3.5% 1m, KO +7.8% 1m/+13.1% 3m), dividend-quality (SCHD +6.0% 1m, +15.2% 6m, +26.0% 12m, +12.4% over 200d), energy (XLE +9.5% 1m, +18.1% 6m), financials (+5.5% 1m).

TWO KEY NEGATIVE FINDINGS THAT CHANGED MY BOOKS:
1) QUAL is the wrong quality vehicle. MSCI USA Quality is heavy in exactly the megacaps de-rating: -0.6% 1m versus XLV +3.4% and SCHD +6.0%. It delivered tech beta, not defense. SCHD's ROE/FCF-and-leverage screen is the same quality factor without the AI-bubble exposure and it beats QUAL on every horizon.
2) Gold is broken, and so are bonds. GLD -22.1% 6m, -4.1% below its 50d and -9.9% below its 200d; GDX -16.7% 3m, SLV -22.3%. The +2.7% gold pop on 7/29 is a bounce inside a confirmed downtrend. TLT is -5.3% 1m with 10y yields at 4.62% and rising. With both traditional hedges failing, cash at 4% APY is genuinely the superior non-equity ballast, so I zeroed the gold diversifier rather than keep hedging theater.

ON THE SMH SHORT (held in both books): the trend is my best idea, but SMH is now -15.5% below its 50-day while still +12.4% ABOVE its 200-day and +70% over 12 months. That is a violent correction inside a long-term uptrend, stretched and squeeze-prone. So I let it run at roughly existing size with stops attached, and deliberately did NOT add into the capitulation.

CRYPTO (Round 3): the trend filter says no. BTC -26.0% 12m, -10.1% 6m, -10.6% below its 200d. ETH -32.4% 12m, -11.7% 6m, -9.7% below its 200d — though ETH is +8.6% above its 50d and +10.0% 1m, the strongest short-term crypto momentum. Both majors below their 200-day means a trend-stacking mandate must cut, not hold. Also cut MTUM entirely (-15.7% 1m, -10.5% below its 50d) and cut JEPI hard — it is -2.9% over 6m, +0.1% over 12m and below its 200-day, i.e. dead money that only earns its keep as the option-carry mandate leg. Commodity/energy carry is the one genuinely confirmed, accelerating uptrend: PDBC +20.2% 6m/+30.2% 12m and +12.6% over its 200d, XLE +18.1% 6m/+33.8% 12m.
